<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `50fd681ea1d398d232fe704c87edc590484ac692` — the merge of head `6c52a63bd1e8b4c9fb59c366299a26b6f5650d10` into base `68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 50fd681ea1d398d232fe704c87edc590484ac692 && git checkout 50fd681ea1d398d232fe704c87edc590484ac692
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4 6c52a63bd1e8b4c9fb59c366299a26b6f5650d10 && git checkout -B drift-repro 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4 && git merge --no-ff 6c52a63bd1e8b4c9fb59c366299a26b6f5650d10

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 68ffa5dc1af1abeb012cd1ed7dfa18be4c07a8c4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review — PR #23962 (card #23904) · 2026-10-16T15:10Z

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9fad187b5013b4868e7a647b0e44b434b1cb4920`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card #23904 (body and all five comments, 6215481679 through 6217917388), PR #23962 (body, its 14-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge-base 11fea6b000), and the 41 check-runs on the head (all concluded). Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here. The logs behind the failed check-runs are not readable without credentials, so each is judged on its conclusion, which is the gate verdict.

### Gate verdicts on this head (the check-runs)

- 32 success, 6 skipped (path-filtered lanes, expected), **3 failure**: the two shards below and the aggregate `Test Core` context branch protection requires. Every lane has concluded.
- **Test Core (1/6) — failure**: `pnpm run test` in `packages/spec` exited 1 (job 117028249972).
- **Test Core (5/6) — failure**: `pnpm run test` in `packages/objectql` exited 1 (job 117028250035).
- **Test Core (aggregate) — failure**, the required context, carrying the two shards. Test Core (2/6), (3/6), (4/6) and (6/6) success. Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, every Lint and Type Check lane, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected: success.
- These are the two packages whose full suites the dev's report (6217917388, deviation 2) declares as "CI's on the PR": spec ran the conversions, migrations and page subsets locally, objectql a registry, artifact and manifest-door subset of its 409 test files. The red therefore sits on exactly the ground local verification did not cover, and the gate verdict decides: **FAIL on this head**. Whether the two reds are the diff's or a pre-existing flake cannot be read from here; the next head must show both shards green, or name the failing files and show them red on `main` too.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **spec — two D2 entries** `page-is-default-off-record-page-removed` and `page-template-full-width-to-default` (`toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, order 67, id-sorted into `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS`). **Right.** Both rewrites are lossless: nothing read a misplaced `isDefault` (the liveness row's own evidence), and `full-width` and `default` resolve to the one `FullWidthTemplate` at the objectui pin (the `template` row's evidence, already on `main`). The strip reuses the parse's one judge, `misplacedDefaultPageRefusal`, so conversion and refusal cannot disagree about which pages are misplaced. `17.7.0` is the newest stable below the `18.0.0-next.2` label, which the retired-after census requires under a prerelease label.
2. **spec — the stored-row seam widens** (`applyConversionsToStoredItem('page', …)`): a stored page carrying the misplaced flag or `full-width` reads back converted and valid with an `OS_METADATA_CONVERTED` notice, where it was badged `_diagnostics.valid: false`. **Right** — this is the card's Wanted and the maintainer's order, 「内核构建遇到已安装、已存储的旧元数据里被退役的声明时，按过渡窗口只警告、不拒绝启动；发布时照样拒」.
3. **spec — the authoring funnel is unchanged**: both entries are retired from the day they land, so `definePage`, `defineStack` (`os validate`, `os build`), the save door and publish refuse the same shapes with the same sentence (pinned in both new entry tests and in `page-default-and-region-placement.test.ts`). **Right** — the 「发布时照样拒」 half.
4. **spec — the artifact file doors widen** for an artifact whose declared floor is at or below 17.7.0 (MetadataPlugin, AppPlugin, `loadArtifactBundle`): the two shapes convert before the strict parse, as every retired entry does. **Right.** HotCRM 4.0.1 stays refused at those doors on the shapes with no lossless rewrite (`centered`, `utility-bar`, the two unplaced regions) and on three ADR-0055 objects older than #23708 — declared in the PR, not widened; correct under Prime Directive 12, since a conversion may only rewrite a shape it positively names.
5. **spec — the `pageAssignedProfilesRemoved` fixture** loses `isDefault: true` on its `team_home` control page in both halves. **Right**: an untyped, unbound page with the flag is now a page the new entry strips, so the pair would have stopped proving "a page with nothing to strip keeps its identity"; no behaviour moves.
6. **metadata-core — `applyArtifactForwardConversions` reads the declared range off a flat body** when the definition carries no `manifest` object. **Right, and no existing door moves**: the three production callers (MetadataPlugin's stack definition, AppPlugin's `{ ...manifest, ...collections }` which still carries `collections.manifest`, and `convertArtifactAtLoad` on the raw file) all hand in a definition with a `manifest`; the only flat caller is the new registration door. The one narrowing the reading implies — a flat body declaring a current-or-newer floor yet carrying a retired shape was under the undeclared amnesty before and answers to the strict parse now — is the versioned-window posture ADR-0087 asks for ("versioned rather than a blanket amnesty"), is pinned in the new metadata-core case, and has no honest producer (`os build` refuses the shape at that floor). Not a second arm.
7. **objectql — `ObjectQL.registerApp` converts a range-declaring body before anything of it registers** (`convertPackageBodyForward`). The accept set widens at the kernel's package registration door for a body with `engines.protocol` below the runtime label: the whole retired chain replays (every D2 entry, not only the two page entries), one `warn` per (package, conversion) naming the id, the floor and the first site, deduped per process. **Right**: this is the one door every registration reaches (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage` and the item seam both sit behind it); the policy function is the same one the artifact doors call, never a second table; it is copy-on-write and idempotent, so a body an artifact door already converted comes back by reference with no second notice. The gate on a declared range is right too: no in-repo code-authored `manifest.register` or `registerApp` body (apps/account, setup, studio, mcp, metadata-protocol) declares `engines`, so code manifests keep today's refusals. Cost: one extra chain walk per registration of an already-converted artifact body — acceptable, and declared.
8. **objectql — the CONTROL refusals hold**: a range-less body and a body declaring a floor newer than every retirement still meet `MisplacedDefaultPageError` (422, the same sentence); `registerItem('page', …, pkgId)` still refuses. **Right**, pinned in the new file and untouched in `registry-default-record-page.test.ts`.
9. **objectql — the `manifest` service converts a whole option-B artifact (`packages[]`) before `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` strict-parses its bodies.** **Right**: one window read off the artifact's own range, every body replayed under it (`replayPackageBodies`), a single-body payload handed through to `registerApp` untouched, a bundle an artifact door already converted returned by reference.
10. **objectql — public surface**: `convertPackageBodyForward(body)` added on the class (not on `IObjectQLEngine`); `registerApp`'s first parameter renamed, type unchanged. Additive, so minor is the right level.
11. **Liveness ledger** (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`): notes only, state counts unchanged, gate green. **Right.** The two D3 entries' prose names the data-at-rest halves and their `conversionIds` stay empty (the authoring surface keeps no mechanical edit). **Right**, and pinned.
12. **Fixture** `hotcrm-4.0.1-published-pages.artifact.json`: the v4.0.1 tag's `dist/objectstack.json` built with its own pinned 17.7.0 toolchain, trimmed to the manifests plus the full `pages` collection (8 pages, declared floor `^17.7.0`). Matches the card's acceptance source ("the v4.0.1 tag's dist/objectstack.json"); read from inside its own package. **Right.** 1380 of the PR's 2235 added lines are this file.
13. **Acceptance as the card words it**: a kernel from the 4.0.1 bundle boots with the named warning (new objectql test, both at the engine door and through `manifest.register`); the authoring door still refuses (the controls); an ablation turns the boot red (PR body, Readings 6: both the entry and the door, restore proven). **Met on the dev's own run** — but the two suites that would confirm it in CI are the red shards above.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23904-installed-page-retired-declarations-convert-at-load.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-core` minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the ADR-0087 marker present and naming both entries; a FROM → TO door table and a `Migration:` line.
- **The level matches what the diff publishes**: the three packages whose published source moves are exactly the three graded; `yes` takes at least minor and gets it; nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no tombstone is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The `!` on the first line is the launch-window spelling (breaking ships as minor, the convention across the current `.changeset/` corpus) — over-declared if anything, since no author's input breaks; harmless, and the body carries what a breaking changeset must.
- **`Clause-②:` line**: `yes (widening)` on the PR body, in the changeset, and matching the claim (6216456972) and triage (6215783095). The direction is right: every door that moves widens its accept set at load; the one narrowing named in ①.6 has no producer and is the intended versioned-window posture, not a second arm. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev's flags (report 6217917388: deviations, open_questions, out-of-scope findings), each answered or escalated:

- **Open question 1 — which chain cloud's KernelManager uses** (`manifest.register` / `registerApp`, now covered, against a direct `registry.installPackage` through `protocol.installPackage` or the `sys_packages` hydration, not covered). Answered: the dev's inference stands as far as this repository can read it — the hydration loop catches and continues, so it cannot have produced "kernel build failed", and the strict-parse doors would have named a Zod issue at `pages.N.template` first, so the covered door is the measured one. Escalated to the seat, two items: the cloud-side confirmation belongs to cloud#2868's pin bump (the dev's own first choice); and the two direct callers (`services/service-package` hydration, `protocol.installPackage`) are rehydration seams the ADR-0087 addendum binds, which today drop a stored package silently after restart — a contract violation under Prime Directive 10, to be filed by the seat as its own card (the dev's class-b finding, carrier none). Not the in-registry door the dev also weighed: a second judge inside the primitive is the shape the ADR forbids.
- **Open question 2 — artifact-door posture for shapes with no lossless rewrite.** Answered: leave as landed. No measured producer needs that door for 4.0.1 (refused there anyway on ADR-0055 objects older than #23708), a conversion may only rewrite a shape it positively names, and turning the strict-parse door into warn-and-serve is a door-policy decision for the maintainer — the card's own "return needs_decision, do not build it" clause. Nothing to escalate until a producer is measured.
- **Open question 3 — the registration window for a range-less body.** Answered: keep it closed, as landed. At this door a range-less manifest is a plugin's code-authored one (every in-repo caller, ①.7), and every `os build` artifact declares its range; the file doors' undeclared amnesty is for a file of unknown age, which a code manifest is not.
- **Deviation 1** (HotCRM 4.0.1 built in a read-only sister clone without the verify lock): a sister repository's own toolchain build, not this repository's build or test — accepted.
- **Deviation 2** (local scope narrowed; the full spec and objectql suites "are CI's on the PR"): this is where the head fails — both suites are red in CI. Not accepted on this head; see the gate verdicts.
- **Deviations 3 to 7** (the dev-prereqs scan form not run; the mutated-leg dist preflight exit 4 explained by the id surviving as D3 prose, with the 8 to 2 hit drop plus the red suite as the reading; the liveness mis-edit corrected against the base file in a later commit; cloud source unreadable; read-only clones removed): declared and explained, no escalation.
- **Out-of-scope finding 2** (`cloud-connection`'s marketplace install side readers `bindArtifactHandlers` and `applySideEffects` read the raw ledger entry): pre-existing and not a page concern; for the seat's dedupe list, not this PR.
- **Governed surfaces**: none in the file list (`.changeset/` and `packages/**` only); Governed Surface Queue Guard success. Not HotCRM, cloud, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**` or `.claude/**` — the claim's file surface held, with the engine files on the cross-domain exception path triage named.

What turns this to PASS on the next head: Test Core (1/6) and (5/6) green, so the aggregate `Test Core` context concludes success — or the failing files named and shown red on `main` too. Sections ① to ③ stand unless the fix for the red moves a door.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23904-installed-page-load-warning`
Reviewed-by: `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review — PR #23962 (card #23904) · 2026-10-16T16:15Z · delta review after FAIL 6218504915

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6c52a63bd1e8b4c9fb59c366299a26b6f5650d10`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read, and nothing else: card #23904 (body and all six comments, 6215481679 through the round-2 dev report 6219350488), PR #23962 (body, its 17-file list, the earlier record 6218504915, the delta `9fad187b` → `6c52a63b` and the net diff against `main` at merge-base `11fea6b000`), and the 41 check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here.

### Gate verdicts on this head (the check-runs)

- 41 check-runs, every one concluded: **35 success, 6 skipped** (path-filtered lanes: Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the dogfood matrix, the opt-in tarball smoke), **0 failure**.
- The five required contexts, by name: `Lint & Repo Gates` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success, `Test Core` success (shards 1/6 through 6/6 all success — the two shards 6218504915 failed on, 1/6 spec and 5/6 objectql, are green), `Build Core` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success. Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Check PR Size, the claim and single-writer guards: success.
- The ground of the FAIL is gone: both reds were this PR's own, as the round-2 report reads them off the job logs (the removal-version pin's JOIN rule, which fires only for entries this PR adds; the save-door pins of #23610 that this PR's data-at-rest conversion changes by design), and both suites were reproduced green locally by the dev at this head (spec 687 files / 20915 tests, objectql 435 files / 8221 tests) before CI confirmed them.

### ① Derived judgments

The delta (three files, +44 / −13) moves no door; sections ① to ③ of 6218504915 stand for the net diff, re-read here against the head, and the three judgments the delta adds are these:

1. **spec — the refusal sentence `misplacedDefaultPageRefusal` now names the release, in both variants** ("… is refused on a `type: 'home'` page since @objectstack/spec 18: …" and "… bound to no `object` since @objectstack/spec 18: …"). **Right, and it reaches every door that prints it**: the sentence has ONE producer (`ui/default-record-page.ts`), and every door prints that producer's return — the page parse (`checkPageDefaultPlacement`, `page.zod.ts:1563`, so `definePage`, `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build` and the metadata save door), the package door (`misplacedDefaultPages` → `refuseDefaultRecordPageConflicts`, `objectql/default-record-page.ts:149`) and the item seam (`registry.ts:4651`). `git grep` at the head finds no hard-coded copy of the sentence in `packages/**`, `content/docs/**`, `skills/**` or the pinned `../objectui`; every existing pin asserts the prefix up to "page" / "object" or the function's own return, so none moved (shards 1/6 and 5/6 green say the same). A release name is not a tracker number, so `check:doc-authoring` (Lint & Repo Gates, green) is not crossed. The naming is required, not cosmetic: the removal-version class pin holds every prescription of an entry retired after the newest published stable (`retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, which IS the newest stable under the `18.0.0-next` label, so `removalMajor` derives `@objectstack/spec 18`) to name exactly that release — the `template: 'full-width'` enum prescription already did ("was removed in @objectstack/spec 18", on `main` since #23708), and this delta brings the `isDefault` sentence level with it.
2. **spec — the JOIN rows** (`retired-key-removal-version.pin.test.ts`): `page-is-default-off-record-page-removed` joined to the two refusals an author meets at `isDefault` (a `type: 'home'` page; a record page bound to no object — the two branches of the one judge), `page-template-full-width-to-default` joined to the enum refusal at `template`. **Right**: each row is "the tombstones or refusals an author meets for its surface", as the pin's own failure text asks; each is rendered by a real `PageSchema.safeParse` at the key, so the row fails the day the parse stops refusing; and the pin's derivation (newest stable 17.7.0 on the v18 train ⇒ 18) is exercised in both directions by the existing rows.
3. **objectql — the repinned stored-row save-door reads** (`default-record-page-save-door.test.ts`, both kernel topologies): a `sys_metadata` page row laid in the store with no write door in front of it (`storeRow` → `driver.create`) is read back through `protocol.getMetaItem` CONVERTED for the two shapes with a lossless rewrite (`isDefault` absent on the home page; `template: 'default'` where `full-width` was stored), served AS STORED for the unplaced `left_sidebar` region (no lossless rewrite, no conversion touches it), and re-saving the row as it was stored is refused 422 in every case. **Right — this is exactly the posture the card and the ADR-0087 data-at-rest addendum require.** The addendum (2026-07-31): "Every stored-row rehydration seam replays the FULL chain, retired entries included — `applyConversionsToStoredItem` … called by … `getMetaItem`" and "Writes stay gated; reads diagnose, never drop. `saveMetaItem` keeps rejecting off-spec bodies (422, tombstones included)". The card, in the maintainer's words: 「内核构建遇到已安装、已存储的旧元数据里被退役的声明时，按过渡窗口只警告、不拒绝启动；发布时照样拒」. The old pins ("read serves the row as stored") were #23610's record of "no D2 conversion", which this PR's D2 entries replace by design; the third shape's pin (served as stored, still refused at save) is unchanged, and it is what the addendum says of a row that still fails the schema after conversion (registered anyway, badged `_diagnostics`). Re-saving the CONVERTED body is the healing round-trip the 2026-08-02 addendum describes, and the authoring refusal of the stored shape is the 「发布时照样拒」 half.

Carried from 6218504915, re-read on this head, each still right: the two D2 entries (`toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`, order 67, lossless both; the strip reuses the parse's one judge); the stored-row seam widening (the card's Wanted); the authoring funnel unchanged (both entries retired from the day they land, pinned "never replays on the authoring funnel"); the artifact file doors widening only inside the versioned window, HotCRM 4.0.1 still refused there on the shapes with no lossless rewrite and on three ADR-0055 objects older than #23708; the `pageAssignedProfilesRemoved` fixture losing a flag the new entry would now strip; metadata-core reading a FLAT body's range off itself with the one narrowing (a flat body at a current-or-newer floor answers to the strict parse, not the undeclared amnesty) pinned and producer-less; `ObjectQL.registerApp` converting a range-declaring body before anything registers, one `warn` per (package, conversion), copy-on-write and idempotent, range-less bodies and floors past every retirement still refused (CONTROL pins, the item seam included); the `manifest` service converting a whole `packages[]` artifact once before `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`; the additive public surface (`convertPackageBodyForward`, `registerApp`'s parameter renamed with its type unchanged); the liveness notes (state counts unchanged, gate green); the D3 prose naming the data-at-rest halves with `conversionIds` still empty; the fixture being the v4.0.1 tag's own build trimmed to manifests plus the full `pages` collection; and the card's three acceptance lines met — the kernel from the 4.0.1 bundle boots with the named warning (new objectql file, engine door and `manifest.register`), the authoring door still refuses (controls), the ablation of entry and door turns the boot red (PR body Readings 6, restore proven) — now with the two suites that carry those pins green in CI.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23904-installed-page-retired-declarations-convert-at-load.md`, unchanged in the delta: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/metadata-core` minor; `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the ADR-0087 marker naming both entries (`check:adr-0087-registration` green); a door table and a `Migration:` line.
- **The level matches what the diff publishes**: the three packages whose published source moves are exactly the three graded; `yes` takes at least minor and gets it; nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no tombstone is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The delta's one published change — the `isDefault` refusal sentence gaining a release name — is a prescription improvement inside `@objectstack/spec`'s minor, not a surface change. The `!` on the first line is the launch-window spelling the current `.changeset/` corpus uses (`check:changeset-no-major` green) — over-declared, harmless.
- **`Clause-②:` line**: `yes (widening)` on the PR body and in the changeset, matching the claim (6216456972) and triage (6215783095). The direction is right: every door that moves widens its accept set at load; the one narrowing (①, metadata-core) has no producer and is the versioned-window posture, not a second arm. **Right.**
- One prose nit, no verdict weight: the changeset's and the PR body's door table says the authoring doors refuse "with the same sentence" — after this delta the `isDefault` sentence carries one more clause (the release name); the refusal, its key and its status are the same. The seat may tighten the word at landing or leave it; the CHANGELOG reader's question (is the refusal unchanged?) is answered correctly either way.
